newsitem.title: USA: CHINA MUST RESTRUCTURE ECONOMY FOR WTO - EIZENSTAT.
newsitem.headline: CHINA MUST RESTRUCTURE ECONOMY FOR WTO - EIZENSTAT.

text.p: China needs to restructure its economy to qualify to join the World Trade Organization, but easing the rules would set a negative precedent for other would-be members, a State Department official said on Friday.

Stuart Eizenstat, Undersecretary of State for commercial and business affairs, said China needed to show commitment to open up its markets, cut tariffs and other trade barriers and eliminate export subsidies.

"It really is in their hands. If they take the steps...then they can become members," he told Reuters Financial Television. "They have have the political will to significantly restructure their economy."
Eizenstat said the United States was ready to allow China a transitional period to meet WTO rules, but not to ease the regulations.
"If China is let in on an artficial basis one would have created a very negative precedent for countries like Vietnam and Russia," he said.
Both Vietnam and Russia are also seeking membership of the WTO, which aims to liberalize trade and open up markets.
